title: Qt: [Re]start the stats when filling the interface list
description:
Use the welcome mode to fill in the interface list and start
the stats at the same time, instead of two calls.

Also now restart the stats when refreshing the interface list
because an interface has changed.

Add a comment that there are still some situations where we don't
trigger an interface refresh on a interface monitor notification
on Linux

Related to #15082

Startup is stuck at "Finding local interfaces" on my macOS M2.

Probably something going on with reading from the sync pipe from dumpcap in `capture/capture_sync.c`, maybe similar to #19349, maybe different. That seems like the most likely place for it to hang.

If you build without the commit, do the sparklines work?

Yes, I get the sparklines.

> Startup is stuck at "Finding local interfaces" on my macOS M2.

And on my macOS Ventura Intel Core i9.

```
    +                 2406 __wait4  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 10  [0x7ff8028f41fe]
```

So `pipe_read_block` returned an error condition.

Hmm, so even though there's that preexisting comment

> We don't have to worry about killing the child, if the sync pipe returned an error. Usually this error is caused as the child killed itself while going down. Even in the rare cases that this isn't the case, the child will get an error when writing to the broken pipe the next time

Maybe we should call `sync_pipe_close_command(` instead or at least close the sync pipe reader to get the child to stop.
There are some `ws_debug` messages in `pipe_read_block` so compiling a Debug release build and running with `--log-level=debug` should give some clues.

Boosting `SP_MAX_MSG_LEN` to 16384 fixes the hang, but if I try to capture on en0, I get the error "Unable to set data link type on interface 'en0' (NULL is not one of the DLTs supported by this device)."  (which is a true statement, as only lo0 would support `DLT_NULL`).

So, first step should be to increase `SP_MAX_MSG_LEN` then.

I'll try to take a look at the other issue.

The first line of output from `dumpcap -S -D -L -Z none` is rather long, as it's a JSON dump of all the interfaces on a single line.

And that's just on my Mac laptop, with various weirdo interfaces that macOS provides; what if somebody does a capture on a server with a large number of ordinary interfaces?

And here's the JSON output, run through a JSON pretty-printer:

[interface-json.txt](/uploads/a6b9f57d400276d1e14b04e4f0591395/interface-json.txt)
One option is trying to increase the length further, but it might make sense to break it up into multiple messages, one for just the interfaces, and then separate JSON objects each interfaces DLTs.

On Windows (but not Linux) I can duplicate the second error by double-clicking on an interface from the welcome page, it doesn't happen if I click on the capture icon that brings up the capture options dialog, so that narrows it down.

For what it's worth, Linux loopback devices provide Ethernet link-layer headers, so they have the same link-layer type as Ethernet devices, but BSD-style (\*BSD and macOS) and Windows loopback devices provide non-Ethernet link-layer headers.

> one for just the interfaces, and then separate JSON objects each interfaces DLTs.

What about other per-interface arrays, such as network addresses?

(And note that, in the future, libpcap may support extensible lists of settable options, as well as providing interface characteristics in pcapng style, so also extensible.  Make no assumptions about what a set of interface settable options and properties will be, other than something that can probaby be represented as JSON.)

Theoretically the sync pipe max message length could go up to 2^24 with the current design, which should accommodate anything within reason, so long as the reader does keep draining the pipe appropriately.
!13785 should fix the unable to set the DLT type issue.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -1020,6 +1020,27 @@ iface_mon_event_cb(const char *iface, int added, int up)
         /*
          * We've been told that there's a new interface or that an old
          * interface is gone; reload the local interface list.
+         *
+         * XXX: We also want to reload the local interface list if [what
+         * we can retrieve about] the capabilities of the device have changed.
+         * Ideally we'd update the capabilities of just the one device in
+         * the cache and signal that the list has been updated, instead of
+         * freeing the entire cache and scanning again - but some extcaps
+         * depend on other interfaces being up; e.g. by default androiddump
+         * tries to connect to the loopback interface to look for adb running,
+         * so if the loopback interface changes so does the status of
+         * androiddump.
+         *
+         * On Linux, at least, you can't get the capabilities from a down
+         * interface, but it's still present in all_ifaces - dumpcap returns
+         * it in the list, and we show it so the user can get a status / error
+         * message when trying to capture on it instead of it vanishing.
+         * So if both present and up are true, then we still want to refresh
+         * to update the capabilities and restart the stats.
+         *
+         * We also store the address in all_ifaces and show them to the user,
+         * so we probably should monitor those events as well and update
+         * the interface list appropriately when those change.

commits_data.message:
Qt: [Re]start the stats when filling the interface list

Use the welcome mode to fill in the interface list and start
the stats at the same time, instead of two calls.

Also now restart the stats when refreshing the interface list
because an interface has changed.

Add a comment that there are still some situations where we don't
trigger an interface refresh on a interface monitor notification
on Linux

Related to #15082
